statement: A capital letter is written on a card. Ana turns the card halfway round, flat on the table, so the top is at the bottom. Which letter looks exactly the same?

choices.misconception: I checked that A matches when folded down the middle and thought that meant it looks the same after a half turn.
I flipped the E over from top to bottom, like a mirror, instead of spinning it round.
I pictured M turned round and thought it was still an M.
I thought a V turned round is still a V.

hints: Try writing each letter on a scrap of paper and turning the paper round.
A half turn spins the letter round its middle, so the top goes to the bottom and the left goes to the right at the same time. This is not the same as folding or flipping it.
Spin each letter in your head. M becomes a W and V becomes an upside-down V. Look at N.

solutions.reliable: Spinning by a half turn moves the top to the bottom and the left to the right. A, M and V end up pointing the other way, and E ends up facing backwards. N spun round is still N. The idea to keep: a half turn is not a fold, so a letter can match one and not the other.

whyOnTest: Students often mix up folding symmetry with turning symmetry, and this question separates the two.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
